sections.title: The Benefits of Target Date Fund Consulting

body.text: Selecting a recognizable fund family isn't the same as documenting a prudent selection process. We help your committee establish clear evaluation criteria, compare alternatives, document the rationale behind the decision, and maintain an ongoing review process.

Two workforces can have very different ages, turnover patterns, savings rates, and retirement behaviors. We evaluate your participant demographics alongside the TDF's assumptions to determine whether the investment strategy is an appropriate fit.

As a fee-only fiduciary with no recordkeeper affiliations or proprietary products, PointOak can evaluate target date fund options objectively. We consider costs, underlying investments, vehicle structure, asset allocation, and other factors rather than simply accepting the recordkeeper's default fund family.

items.title: A Clearer Custom vs. Off-the-Shelf Decision

body.text: A custom target date strategy can provide greater control, but it also requires greater governance. We help determine whether the additional complexity is justified by your plan size, participant demographics, available investment vehicles, and fiduciary capacity.

Target date fund selection isn't a one-time exercise. Glide paths change, fees move, investment teams evolve, and your workforce changes. We establish an ongoing monitoring process so your committee can periodically confirm that the selected strategy continues to fit the plan.

Selecting a target date fund requires more than comparing performance. We evaluate participant demographics, costs, underlying investments, asset allocation, and overall fund structure to help determine which TDF series best fits your plan.

Funds with the same target year can take very different levels of risk. We evaluate how each TDF shifts from equities to more conservative investments over time and whether that glide path reflects how your participants are likely to save, retire, and withdraw assets.

Does your plan need a custom target date strategy, or would a well-selected off-the-shelf series provide the right balance of fit, cost, and simplicity? We evaluate both approaches using your plan's actual participant profile and governance needs.

sections.title: Who Benefits Most from Target Date Fund Consulting?

items.title: Your Current TDF Was Selected by the Recordkeeper

body.text: If the fund series was inherited, automatically added, or selected without an independent comparison, your committee may benefit from a documented suitability review.
A provider transition creates an opportunity to reassess TDF options, investment vehicles, fees, and share classes before simply carrying the existing lineup into the new platform.

items.title: Your Workforce Doesn't Fit Generic Assumptions

body.text: Unusual age distributions, high employee turnover, concentrated salary ranges, or participant behavior may make a standard glide path less appropriate for your plan.

Custom solutions can offer greater flexibility, but they also introduce additional governance and monitoring responsibilities. An independent analysis can determine whether the added complexity creates enough value to justify it.

items.title: Your Committee Is Concerned About QDIA Oversight

body.text: If your committee isn't confident it could explain why the current TDF was selected and how it is monitored, a formal review can strengthen both the decision and its documentation.

items.title: When a Separate TDF Engagement May Not Be Necessary

body.text: If your plan has straightforward demographics, a recently documented independent review, competitive fees, and a clear ongoing monitoring process, your existing investment oversight may be sufficient.

sections.title: Off-the-Shelf vs. Custom Target Date Funds

blocks.text: Both approaches can work well. The better choice depends on your participant population, plan size, available investment vehicles, cost structure, and governance capacity.

A custom structure isn't automatically better. Our role is to determine whether the additional flexibility is useful for your plan—or whether a carefully selected off-the-shelf TDF offers a better combination of fit, cost, and governance simplicity.

items.q: What is target date fund consulting?

a.text: Target date fund consulting helps plan fiduciaries evaluate, select, document, and monitor the TDF series used within their retirement plan.

A comprehensive review considers participant demographics, glide path, underlying investments, fees, vehicle structure, and ongoing monitoring requirements rather than relying solely on the fund's target year.

items.q: How do you choose the right target date fund for a 401(k)?

a.text: Start by evaluating the plan's participants, then compare the funds' glide paths, asset allocations, fees, underlying investments, and overall structure.
The goal is to identify a strategy that reasonably fits your workforce and document why the committee selected it.
A glide path shows how a target date fund's asset allocation changes as participants approach and move through retirement.
Funds with the same target year can have significantly different equity exposure and risk levels. Glide path analysis helps determine whether that risk pattern makes sense for your participants.

items.q: What's the difference between a “to” and “through” glide path?

a.text: A “to” glide path generally reaches its most conservative allocation around the target retirement date. A “through” glide path continues changing its allocation after retirement.
Neither approach is universally better. The appropriate structure depends in part on how participants are expected to use their assets after retiring.

items.q: Are all target date funds with the same year basically the same?

a.text: Two 2040 funds, for example, can have different equity exposure, underlying holdings, fees, asset classes, and glide path philosophies. The target year is only one part of the evaluation.

items.q: What's the difference between an off-the-shelf and custom TDF?

a.text: An off-the-shelf TDF uses a prebuilt investment strategy and glide path created for a broad population. A custom TDF can be structured more specifically around a plan's demographics and investment objectives.
Custom strategies also require greater governance, so the additional flexibility needs to justify the additional complexity.

items.q: How often should target date funds be reviewed?

a.text: Target date funds should be reviewed periodically as part of the plan's ongoing investment-monitoring process and whenever significant changes occur.
Changes in fees, management, glide path, fund structure, recordkeepers, or participant demographics can all warrant additional review.

items.q: Does PointOak only review the TDF offered by our recordkeeper?

a.text: PointOak is independent of recordkeepers and proprietary fund providers, allowing us to evaluate available alternatives without an incentive to favor a particular fund family.

items.q: What should our committee document when selecting a TDF?

a.text: The fiduciary record should show what criteria were considered, which alternatives were reviewed, why the selected strategy was appropriate for the plan, and how it will be monitored going forward.
PointOak helps organize that information into a documented process your committee can maintain over time.
